correctness.rationale: At doubling, the physical Lyapunov Hessian for F_t=2x+t w is -σ_D²(w′)/4, with expansion -t²σ_D²(w′)/8. Fourier towers of doubling give σ_D²(g)=2 Σ_(odd m>0)|Σ_j ĝ(2^j m)|², so the zero quadratic-loss degree-two real trigonometric perturbations form C=-A/2, E=-B/2. For v=u∘D-2u the conjugacy Hε(x)=x+εu(x) removes first-order perturbation, leaving Sε=D+ε²(u v′)+O_C5(ε³); first differential vanishes, so fourth-order term is -(ε⁴/8)σ_D²((u v′)′). The independent Fourier convolution of u and v′ recovers σ²=(a²+b²)(9a²+5b²)/16 and coefficient (a²+b²)(9a²+5b²)/128. Symbolic exact checks: (a,b)=(1,0):9/128;(0,1):5/128;(1,1):7/32;(2,1):205/128. Remainder only fixed real (a,b) and sufficiently small ε; no uniform over amplitudes claim.
